_help: Cause & effect explorer. Each event lists typical effects at three levels: local (Western Norway), national (Norway) and international (World). Effects are typical directions, not forecasts.

events.name: Oil price jumps 30%
events.summary: Brent rises sharply, for example after supply disruptions in the Middle East.

effects.label: Supply base activity
effects.text: Oil companies spend more on the shelf. That means more traffic at bases like CCB Ågotnes and Mongstad, and more trucking, warehousing and project logistics serving them.

effects.label: Truck operating cost
effects.text: Diesel is often a quarter to a third of a truck's running cost. Hauliers with a diesel clause pass it on monthly; those without carry the loss until contracts are renegotiated.

effects.label: Oslo-listed tanker & offshore shares
effects.text: Investors expect higher earnings for tanker and offshore companies. Over time, higher oil revenue also tends to support the krone.

effects.label: Bunker cost, sailing speed
effects.text: Fuel costs rise, so ships slow down. Slower ships carry less per year, which tightens supply and can support freight rates.

effects.label: Tanker rates
effects.text: Higher prices can trim oil demand, but if the spike comes from a supply disruption, cargoes travel further and tanker rates often rise.

effects.label: Rig and vessel dayrates
effects.text: Oil companies raise exploration and production budgets. Rig and supply vessel dayrates usually follow, with a lag of 6–18 months.

events.name: Red Sea or Hormuz disrupted
events.summary: Attacks make a key strait unsafe, and ships reroute or wait.

effects.label: Feeder schedules to Bergen
effects.text: Containers to Western Norway usually come via hubs like Rotterdam or Hamburg. When ocean ships arrive late or in bunches, feeder services and local deliveries slip too.

effects.label: Delivery predictability
effects.text: Imported goods arrive later and less evenly. Terminals and hauliers see quiet days followed by peaks when delayed ships arrive together.

effects.label: Norwegian tanker & gas owners
effects.text: Owners with ships trading in the spot market often earn more as routes lengthen, and their share prices react quickly.

effects.label: Container spot rates
effects.text: Going around the Cape of Good Hope makes Asia–Europe voyages roughly a third longer. That absorbs ships, so spot container rates jump and schedules slip.

effects.label: War-risk premiums
effects.text: Insurers charge large additional premiums for the area, and some owners and crews refuse to sail there.

effects.label: Tanker ton-mile demand
effects.text: Oil takes longer routes or comes from more distant suppliers, so each cargo ties up a tanker for longer.

events.name: Norway cuts diesel tax by NOK 1/litre
events.summary: The road usage tax on diesel is reduced.

effects.label: Cost for Western Norway hauliers
effects.text: Long distances and mountain routes make fuel a big cost in Western Norway, so timber, construction and distribution hauliers feel the relief quickly.

effects.label: Haulier margins
effects.text: A truck using 40,000 litres a year saves about NOK 40,000. Hauliers on fixed-price contracts keep the saving; those with diesel clauses pass it on.

effects.label: Incentive to go electric
effects.text: Cheaper diesel weakens the cost case for electric trucks, so expect debate about climate targets and road funding.

events.name: China construction boom
events.summary: Stimulus drives up steel production and raw material imports.

effects.label: Norwegian dry bulk shares
effects.text: Oslo-listed bulker owners earn more, and some pay large dividends in strong markets.

effects.label: Capesize rates
effects.text: More iron ore and coal is imported, mainly on Capesizes from Australia and Brazil. With few spare ships, rates can multiply.

effects.label: Bulker values and orders
effects.text: Higher earnings lift secondhand prices. Owners start ordering newbuildings, which limits how long the upswing lasts.

events.name: Sanctions on an oil exporter
events.summary: Western countries ban services to a major oil exporter's trade.

effects.label: Shadow-fleet risk in Nordic waters
effects.text: Older tankers with unclear insurance sail along the Norwegian coast and through the Baltic approaches. Nordic and Baltic authorities step up checks of their documents.

effects.label: Diesel import cost
effects.text: Fuel imports shift to other suppliers, often farther away, which can push up wholesale diesel prices.

effects.label: Compliant tanker rates
effects.text: Trade reroutes over longer distances and part of the fleet splits off into a shadow fleet, so tankers available for mainstream trades become scarcer.

effects.label: Insurance & finance withdrawal
effects.text: Western insurers and banks must stop covering sanctioned trades, raising oil spill risk for coastal states.

events.name: Interest rates rise 1 percentage point
events.summary: Central banks tighten, and floating-rate loans get more expensive.

effects.label: Truck financing cost
effects.text: Truck loans and leases cost more. Small hauliers with thin margins feel it first, and fleet renewal, including electric trucks, slows down.

effects.label: Nordic bond coupons
effects.text: NOK bonds priced at NIBOR plus a margin cost more for Norwegian shipping and offshore companies.

effects.label: Ship breakeven
effects.text: On a USD 30 million floating-rate loan, one percentage point adds USD 300,000 a year—about USD 820 a day on the breakeven.

effects.label: Newbuilding orders
effects.text: Costlier financing and lower ship values cool ordering, which limits future supply and supports rates later.

events.name: EU carbon price doubles
events.summary: Emission allowances under the EU ETS become twice as expensive.

effects.label: Shore power and green fuels in ports
effects.text: Ports such as Bergen invest more in shore power and alternative fuels, since ships pay for emissions at berth.

effects.label: Coastal and short-sea cost
effects.text: Voyages within the EEA pay for all their emissions, which raises costs for coastal shipping and can shift some cargo between sea and road.

effects.label: Surcharges and speed
effects.text: Carriers pass the cost on through emission surcharges, and ships slow down to burn less fuel.

effects.label: Old vs new ship values
effects.text: Older, less efficient ships lose value, while modern dual-fuel ships earn a premium.

events.name: Wave of newbuilding deliveries
events.summary: Ships ordered in a boom all arrive within a year or two.

effects.label: Freight rates
effects.text: The fleet grows faster than demand, utilisation drops and rates fall—often sharply, towards the level where ships only cover operating costs.

effects.label: Scrapping
effects.text: Owners send older ships to recycling earlier, which partly offsets the new supply.

effects.label: Ship values and covenants
effects.text: Secondhand values fall, and owners with high loan-to-value may breach value maintenance clauses.

events.name: Strike or congestion at European hub ports
events.summary: Rotterdam, Antwerp or Hamburg slow down for weeks.

effects.label: Feeder arrivals in Western Norway
effects.text: Feeder schedules to Bergen and Stavanger slip when the hubs they connect to are congested.

effects.label: Truck and terminal load
effects.text: Containers for Norway arrive late and in bunches, leaving truck capacity idle one week and overloaded the next.

effects.label: Effective container capacity
effects.text: Ships waiting outside ports are effectively removed from supply. Carriers add congestion surcharges and skip ports.

events.name: Key road closure in Western Norway
events.summary: For example night closures of Lærdalstunnelen on the E16.

effects.label: Detours and waiting time
effects.text: Trucks must plan around closure windows or wait for reopening, which can break driving-time plans and delivery slots.

effects.label: Load on alternative routes
effects.text: Some Bergen–Oslo freight moves to other mountain crossings or to rail, which can congest those alternatives.

effects.label: Freight prices on the corridor
effects.text: Longer trips and lost hours raise the cost per trip, which hauliers try to pass on to customers.
